question: As per the 2011 Census, which Union Territory of India has the highest sex ratio (females per 1000 males)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Puducherry**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The number of women and men in a country is an important demographic characteristic.
 
• The ratio between the number of women and men in the population is called the Sex Ratio.
 
• In some countries it is calculated by using the formula:
 
 
• Male Population/ Female Population X 1000 or
 
• the number of males per thousand females.
 
 
 
• In India, the sex ratio is worked out using the formula:
 
 
• Female Population / Male Population × 1000 
 
• or the number of females per thousand males.
 
 
 
• The sex ratio is an important information about the status of women in a country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Kerala has the highest sex ratio in India, according to the 2011 census, with 1084 girls for every 1000 males.
 
• Tamil Nadu ranks second with 996 girls for every 1000 males.
 
• With a sex ratio of 993, Andhra Pradesh ranks third, followed by Chhattisgarh (991) and Meghalaya (989).
 
• With 879 girls for every 1000 males, Haryana has the poorest sex ratio among the states.
 
• The greatest sex ratio among Union Territories is 1037 in Puducherry, while the lowest sex ratio is 618 in Daman and Diu.
